title: Subsidies for private therapy and intensive early intervention for autistic children
asked: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether subsidies could be extended to private speech and occupational therapy providers for autistic children, and what measures are being taken to reduce the financial burden on middle-income families whose children need more intensive therapy than EIPIC provides.
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said ECDA funds EIPIC and EIPIC-P, with means-tested fee caps; a median income family pays up to $210 a month for EIPIC and $360 a month for EIPIC-P. Each child, including those with a confirmed or suspected autism diagnosis, has an Individualised Education Plan, and enrolled children typically receive five to 12 hours of intervention over two or three sessions weekly. Parents can use the Child Development Account to pay for additional early intervention services by ECDA-registered providers. In supplementary replies, he recommended ECDA-registered providers, said the list is comprehensive, and said the ministry is open to reviewing gaps.

key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming

key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming

key_points.quote: Parents who wish to seek supplementary intervention beyond those provided under EIPIC or EIPIC-P may also tap on the Child Development Account (CDA) to pay for additional early intervention services by early intervention providers registered with ECDA.

key_points.point: The Minister strongly recommends that parents use the list of service providers registered with ECDA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we strongly recommend that parents go with the list of service providers registered with ECDA.

key_points.quote: if there are gaps within the list provided by ECDA, based on what the Member has gotten feedback from, we will be open to reviewing it

left_open: Whether subsidies will be extended to private speech and occupational therapy providers
Whether a tiered co-payment model for private providers will be considered

Any new measures to reduce costs for middle-income families needing more intensive therapy beyond existing EIPIC/EIPIC-P and CDA arrangements
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on a tiered co-payment model for private providers and using CDA funds for more accredited private therapies.
